newsitem.title: ITALY: BOI'S Fazio calls for more bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: BOI'S Fazio calls for more bank mergers.

text.p: Italy's inefficient banks need to form alliances at home and abroad in order boost economies of scale and raise profitability, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Saturday.

"Lower profitability is a widespread problem among Italian banks," said Fazio, adding that Italian banks' profits as a proportion of capital and reserves averaged only 1.6 percent between 1993 and 1995.
This compared with 17.1 percent in Britain and 14.9 poercetnin the United States over the same period.
"Only in France is the average profitability of banking capital lower than in Italy," he said.
Mergers would allow banks to invest in advanced techology and to become more competitive internationally.
"An impulse to profitability and to international competitiveness of the big banks can come from mergers with institutions, Italian and foreign, of significant size," said Fazio.
The Italian banking industry is witnessing a trend towards greater concentration.

Banco Ambrosiano Veneto announced recently its merger with savings bank Cariplo. Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and insurer INA are jointly acquiring control of Banco di Napoli, Southern Italy's largest bank.

"The process of concentration is entrusted to the initiative of those responsible for (running) the banks," said Fazio. "The Bank of Italy encourages and accompanies this process," he said. Rome newsroom +396-6782560
